question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(|X|<5)=0.8198,$ find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ | $\,0.8729\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9066\,$ | $\,0.9082\,$ | $\,0.9099\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<5)=P(-5<X<5).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-5<X<5) & =0.8198 \\ 2P(0<X<5) & =0.8198 \\ P(0<X<5) & =0.4099 \\ P(X<5)-P(X<0) & =0.4099 \\ P(X<5)-0.5 & =0.4099 \\ P(X<5) & =0.9099 \\ P(X\le 5) & =0.9099\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =0.9099 \\ P(Z\le \frac{5-0}{\sigma }) & =0.9099 \\ Φ(\frac{5}{\sigma }) & =0.9099 \\ \frac{5}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.9099)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.34)=0.9099\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.9099)=1.34.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sigma } & =1.34 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{5}{1.34} \\ \sigma  & ≈3.73.\end{aligned}
$$
